round: review round 5, answering tester round 9's two failures

proof.criterion: The tester's failure 1: the repository's own suite is green at the head. `legion claims forget-session` prints the same claims table as `legion claims list`, and this change's two new columns, the open round and the head the worker reported, were added to the list's assertion and not to forget-session's.
proof.surface: The `legion` CLI's own test harness, which runs the real command against a real operator daemon over a real Postgres and reads the bytes the command prints.
proof.observed: ok github.com/sjawhar/legion/daemon/cmd/legion 2.764s. The assertion at cmd/legion/claims_test.go:570 now reads the row with both columns, `… failed 3 <contract> - -`, which is the shape the two tests of `claims list` at claims_test.go:477-478 and :634 already read.
proof.negativeControl: The test was red before the change, at code head c3ff95ec11f3, with exactly the tester's output: `forget-session stdout = "legion-legion-legion-208-architect architect LEGION-208 failed 3 44 - -\n", want "… failed 3 44\n"`. The expectation is the only line that changed; the printer was not touched, so the columns the operator reads are the same in both commands, which is what the shared printer promises.

proof.criterion: The tester's failure 2: the branch's own content in docs/kubernetes.md and scripts/e2e/README.md, which the forward merge resolved to main's side and the rescue carry-over did not catch, is back and brought to this head's rules.
proof.surface: The two documents themselves, read against the code they describe, and the repository's own layout checker.
proof.command: cd packages/daemon && grep -n 'until its update round replaces the pod' internal/runtime/sandbox/sandbox.go; for s in warnImageDrift roundCovers shapeDrift movedInPod answerByTurnEnd openPluginUpdate reconcilePluginUpdate; do grep -rln "func .*$s\|$s =" internal/; done; cd .. && bun scripts/semantic-line-breaks.ts docs/kubernetes.md scripts/e2e/README.md
proof.observed: The branch's content is back across four regions of docs/kubernetes.md and three of scripts/e2e/README.md: the update round and when the daemon opens one, the legion.dev/pod-shape annotation and what PodDrift compares, pod_update_retask_hours and pod_update_notice_hours with their defaults, that a launch into a live drifted issue pod keeps it and the round replaces it, and the pod-update and pod-update-fleet checkpoints with their STAGE4A_FROM entry points, which stage4a-sandbox-runtime.sh carries and the README had lost. Every symbol the restored text cites resolves: warnImageDrift's log line is byte for byte sandbox.go:976's, and roundCovers, shapeDrift (runtime/sandbox/drift.go), movedInPod (runtime/sandbox/addresses.go), answerByTurnEnd (supervise/table.go), openPluginUpdate (supervise/plugin.go) and reconcilePluginUpdate (daemon/podupdate.go) each exist where the text says. The layout checker prints nothing and exits 0. The three corrections the architect named are in: the 'pinned only after every tree is drained' rule is gone from both its places, the sentence saying a launch replaces such a pod through imageDrift in relaunch.go is gone with its dependent clause, and no sentence of either file tells an operator to drain for an image, plugin or configuration update.
proof.negativeControl: Three greps, each a case the restoration had to fail if it were only cosmetic: `grep -n 'pinned only after every tree is drained\|imageDrift' docs/kubernetes.md` finds nothing; `grep -c 'pod-shape\|pod_update_retask_hours\|pod_update_notice_hours\|update round' docs/kubernetes.md` is 15, against 0 at the head the tester read; `grep -c 'pod-update' scripts/e2e/README.md` is 5, against 0 there. Every remaining hit of `grep -n -i drain` over both files was read: each is another subject — a connection drain, the cloudsql-iam switch at a pushed boundary, or the one-off cutover from the per-claim Sandbox layout.

proof.criterion: The architect's items 3 and 4: the round's regression command includes ./cmd/legion, and the suites run against a PostgreSQL of this role's own rather than another role's server.
proof.surface: The repository's own Go suite for the whole daemon module, on a server this role started on the issue's volume.
proof.command: export LEGION_TESTPG_DIR=$XDG_DATA_HOME/testpg-infra484 LEGION_TEST_PG_DSN=postgres://legion_test@127.0.0.1:5447/legion_infra484?sslmode=disable && legion-testpg ensure && cd packages/daemon && gofmt -l . && go build ./... && go vet -tags e2e ./... && go test ./internal/... ./cmd/... -count=1 -timeout 30m
proof.observed: legion-testpg serves postgres://legion_test@127.0.0.1:5447/legion_infra484 from /legion/scratch/data/testpg-infra484/data, a database the test role owns, on a port no other role holds. gofmt, go build and go vet -tags e2e clean. The suite leaves exactly eleven failures, the set the tester recorded as this branch's environment since round 2, each reproducing on a clone of main: internal/admit (1), internal/daemon's TestBootReconcileHoldsATodoUnderAnUnreleasedChildOfALiveTree (Docker), internal/intake (1), internal/launcher (2), internal/natsauth (1), internal/runtime/tmux (1), internal/testnats (1), internal/workflow (2) and cmd/legion's TestProbeImageReadsEachRolesOwnOverlaysAsTheRoleStarts (needs the worker image). There is no twelfth, and TestClaimsForgetSessionPostsToTheClaimRoute is green.
proof.negativeControl: The same suite on the shared server was the control the tester already ran and recorded: nineteen failures there, eight of them cross-talk from another role's databases, which vanish on a server of one's own. The private server reproduces the eleven and none of the eight, which is what separates this change's verdict from the pod's.

filesChanged: packages/daemon/cmd/legion/claims_test.go — the forget-session row carries the round and head columns.

docs/kubernetes.md — the branch's content restored across four regions and brought to the no-drain rule; the 'pinned only after every tree is drained' rule and the imageDrift-in-relaunch.go sentence deleted.
scripts/e2e/README.md — the pod-update and pod-update-fleet checkpoint rows restored, and STAGE4A_FROM's entry points for them.
trickyParts: The lost content could not be applied as a patch: main had reformatted both files to semantic line breaks between the branch's edit and this head, so every statement of the old diff had to be found in the new layout and written there in the current file's voice. The old diff is kept for a reader at /legion/scratch/tmp/lost-kubernetes.diff and /legion/scratch/tmp/lost-e2e-readme.diff.

The restoration is not a replay: the lost text predates the owner's direction of 2026-10-31, so its drain paragraph, its 'pinned only after every tree is drained' rule and its sentence about imageDrift replacing a pod at the next launch are all behaviour this change removes. Each was rewritten to the current rule rather than carried across.

A role's own PostgreSQL is `legion-testpg ensure` with LEGION_TESTPG_DIR under the issue's volume and a port of the role's own; `ensure` makes the database the DSN names owned by the test role when that name is not `postgres`, which also removes the `permission denied for schema public` the default DSN gives on PostgreSQL 18.
discoveredComplexity: The forward merge is where the loss happened, and nothing reported it: jj resolved both documents to main's side without a conflict, because main's reformat rewrote every line the branch had touched. The guard that catches it is the unchanged-diff fingerprint read file by file rather than as one hash — the branch's file count fell from 133 to 135 while two files left it, which is what the tester compared.
